mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in CPIAUCSL, predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as higher policy rates discount future earnings.
regime_hint: Rising inflation and tightening policy cycle
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-inflation-spike period (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS increases are not followed by CPIAUCSL declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) above 50,000 jobs, occurring during a period of UNRATE below 6%, is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as hiring momentum boosts corporate earnings expectations.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in a low-unemployment regime
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive such labor months, the 20-day forward returns are negative on average, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (residential construction) of at least 3% followed by a decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by 2% signals a shift from supply-driven to demand-driven growth, predicting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
regime_hint: Transition from supply chain strength to demand recovery
failure_condition: Over 10 such cycles, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than a neutral baseline (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5% in a month when UNRATE is below 4% signals supply-side weakness that compresses corporate profit margins, leading to a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
regime_hint: Weak supply in a low-unemployment environment
failure_condition: In 5 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not negative on average (mean > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 4-month decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% signals disinflation and accommodative policy, forecasting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev(GDPC1) * 0.98 FOR 4 CONSECUTIVE MONTHS AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: Across 10 such disinflation episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a neutral benchmark (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly UNRATE crossing above 7% while PAYEMS remains flat or declining indicates a tightening labor market, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors anticipate earnings compression.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening in a high-unemployment regime
failure_condition: Over 8 such episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time monthly spike in GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeding 2% of the prior month's value, without a corresponding rise in HOUST (residential construction), predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as demand-driven spending supports earnings.
failure_condition: In 10 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 4% in a regime where UNRATE > 4% signals weak consumer demand, resulting in a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
regime_hint: Weak demand in a high-unemployment regime
failure_condition: Across 6 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not negative on average (mean > 0).
